item.text:
**Verdict:** No.

I found no credible 2023 evidence that Putin respected term limits, succession rules, coalition commitments, or a genuine constitutional transfer of power. The closest counterevidence is purely formal: Russia still held elections and maintained the appearance of constitutional procedure, but the field was tightly controlled and opposition challengers were blocked.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Short claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Russia: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report | Freedom House | 2023 | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2023) | Freedom House says the 2020 constitutional changes strengthened presidential control, judges’ careers depend on Kremlin preferences, and the system remains centered on Putin rather than on any real succession rule or institutional transfer. | 4B.8, 4B.4, 4B.5 |
| Russia: Nations in Transit 2023 Country Report | Freedom House | 2023 | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2023) | Freedom House says Russian politics had already become deeply personalist, with local autonomy curtailed and the ruling coalition organized around Putin’s survival rather than orderly succession. | 4B.8, 4B.4, 4B.5 |
| Russia: 2023 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices | U.S. Department of State | 22 Apr 2024 | [link](https://www.state.gov/reports/2023-country-reports-on-human-rights-practices/russia) | The report says authorities punished dissent, restricted political participation, and organized sham elections in occupied Ukrainian territories. That is evidence against any meaningful respect for constitutional transfer or succession rules. | 4B.8, 4B.2, 4B.3 |
| Russians vote in tightly controlled regional elections | Reuters | 9 Sep 2023 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russians-vote-in-tightlycontrolled-regional-elections-first-since-war-began-3169837) | Reuters reported that elections still occurred in 2023, which is the only weak procedural counterevidence. But the same report says the contests were tightly controlled, with opposition candidates blocked and voting practices used to suppress real competition. | 4B.8, 4B.2 |
| Anti-war challenger Duntsova barred from running against Russia’s Putin | Reuters | 23 Dec 2023 | [link](https://theprint.in/world/anti-war-challenger-duntsova-barred-from-running-against-russias-putin/1898291/) | The Central Election Commission rejected a credible anti-war challenger in the run-up to the 2024 presidential race, showing the succession field was being cleared rather than opened. | 4B.8, 4B.2, 4B.3 |
| Russia arrests leader of vote monitoring group three weeks before regional polls | Reuters | 18 Aug 2023 | [link](https://theprint.in/world/russia-arrests-leader-of-vote-monitoring-group-three-weeks-before-regional-polls/1720660/) | Arresting the Golos co-chair and raiding monitors’ homes was an attempt to block scrutiny of the vote, not to support a credible transfer process. | 4B.8, 4B.2, 4B.3 |
| Russia: Nations in Transit 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2024) | Looking back at 2023, Freedom House says electoral integrity worsened because of fraud, intimidation, and the absence of genuine opposition. Its only limited counterpoint is that municipal councils still offered a shrinking training ground for opposition, which is far short of real succession. | 4B.8, 4B.2, 4B.3 |

**Search gap:** I did not find any solid 2023 evidence that Putin accepted term limits, honored succession rules, or prepared a real constitutional handoff. The evidence instead points to managed elections, exclusion of challengers, and a system centered on personal rule.
